newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian/US bond spread finds a cap 100 bp.
newsitem.headline: Australian/US bond spread finds a cap 100 bp.

text.p: The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread brushed 100 basis points for the first time in around a month, although this proved a cap for the market, and initial differential widening was pared.

Domestic bonds underperformed the dollar bloc prior to today's A$900 million Treasury bond tender, although this was seen sufficiently well-supported to lift the market going into the close, traders said.

The onus could now be put on the U.S. market which faces the first leg of the quarterly refunding auctions with the sale of US$17.75 billion of three-year notes and out of a total US$39.75 billion of securities to issued over the next few days.
Meanwhile, New Zealand bonds recouped Monday's spread narrowing against Australia amid swap-related activity in the N.Z. 2004 bond. The Australia/N.Z. 10-year bond yield dropped to parity on Monday.
